DE'CISION NO. 21

DECISION NO. 39

Your Committee on Jurisprudence has considered Decision No. 21
of the Grand Master which was as follows:
W·here an applicant stated in answer to question 6 of the
application that he had not resided in California for the requisite
time. but nevertheless is accepted, elected and receives the 1°.
following which on objection made the applicant is stopped, a
claim being made, however, substantiated by evidence that the
applicant did not have his rights under Ross Digest 238, 239 and
240, what procedure should be followed when the applicant now
desires to proceed? What does he do and what does the Lodge
do?
I have reached the following conclusions:
1. Residence in Masonry must be actual, rather than constructive ( R.D. 684). Therefore, applicant's original petition
ruled out the possibility of residence. The Victorville Lodge overlooked this fact and accepted applicant.
2. But that Lodge having assumed jurisdiction, applicant's
lack of residence does not affect his present status as an Entered
A·pprentice (R.D. 691 ).
3. The Lodge, after committee recommendation, apparently
voted to sustain the objection (Oct. 6, 1946). The fact that the
subject was denied certain of his rights under R.D. Sec. 238-9-40
should certainly require a proper reconsideration by the Lodge,
if the subject so desires or so requests.
4. If the applicant does not care to question the procedure,
however, but accepts the action of the Lodge sustaining the objection, he now has two alternatives:
(a) He may submit his petition with fee to Victorville Lodge.
( b) He may submit his regular petition to the Lodge where he
presently resides (with fee) and request them to obtain consent and waiver of jurisdiction from Victorville Lodge.
( c) These petitions must be processed and voted on in the regular manner (unanimous).
See Sections 818-819, Ross Digest.
The Committee recommends approval of the above Decision with
conclusion 3 being modified as follows:
"The Lodge, after committee recommendation, apparently
voted to sustain the objection (Oct. 6, 1946). The fact that the
subject was denied certain of his rights under R.D. Sec. 238-9-40,
should certainly require a proper reconsideration by the .Lodge,
if the subject so desires or so requests, after being so notified."
and with the understanding by the Committee that the objection was
made on the grounds of un-Masonic conduct.
Adopted.

NOMINATION OF COMMISSIONERS
Near the end of our last Annual Communication, amid a modicum
of confusion, a resolution, which we were erroneously informed had the
approval of the Committee on Grievances, came before this Committee
and upon our recommendation was adopted. Said resolution reversed
the decision of Grand Master Johnson rendered in 1892 (Sec. 974
Ross Digest) which permitted nomination of trial commissioners. To
rectify t~e error Brother Joe.L. Shell, P.M., San Diego Lodge No. 35
and Chairman of the Committee on Grievances has presented a resolution to permit nomination of trial commissioners through amendment
of our Ordinances.
Since Brother Shell's resolution would restore longstanding law

APPEAL BY RALPH A. BURKE
Section 260 of our Ordinances provides, among other things, that:
"Should any member suspended for non-payment of dues neglect for
the period of two years to pay said dues or to have the same remitted
by his Lodge, said member shall not be restored except by a two-thirds,
vote by ballot of all the members present * * * ."
In 1933, presumably following the procedure prescribed in sections
257-258 of our Ordinances, Chico Lodge No. 111 suspended Ralph A.
Burke from all rights and privileges of Masonry, for non-payment of
dues.
Twelve years later (in October, 1945) Burke's application for
restoration was rejected by unanimous ballot;
After more than eight years he again applied for restoration and
was similarly rejected in April, 1954;

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

357

In April, 1955, a fourth application for restoration was made which
was likewise rejected on May 10, 1955.
July 31, 1955, Burke filed with the Grand Secretary a paper designated as an "appeal" wherein he asks that the Lodge's action of May
l 0, 1955, be reversed and that he be restored to all the rights and
privileges of Masonry, including rights as a member and Past Master
of Chico Lodge No. 111.
While characterized as an "appeal" the document actually seeks
revocation by the Grand Lodge of the ballot of the Lodge on Burke's
application for restoration.
No irregularity, fraud or other misconduct being claimed, full faith
and credit must be given to the Lodge's action as shown by the record,
and your committee recommends that the petition be denied.
We, therefore, offer the following resolution and move its adoption:
RESOLVED: That the foregoing described action on the part
of Chico Lodge No. 111 be approved and that the application
of Ralph A. Burke to reverse said action and be restored to all the
rights and privileges of Masonry be denied.
Adopted.

RESTORATION BY GRAND LODGE
Your Committee on Jurisprudence has carefully and thoroughly
considered the proposed amendments to Section 344 and 345 of Ross
Digest, and concedes that they possess substantial logical merit. Nevertheless, it is the unanimous opinion of your Committee that for the
following reasons, the proposed amendments be not adopted:
1. They will take away from the constituent lodges a portion of the
jurisdiction and control they have traditionally exercised over
their members in the most important area of dues and lodge
financing.
2. They are likely to result in a loss of income to the constituenl
Lodges. Upon restoration by Grand Lodge, the brother becomes
a Mason in good standing, entitled to all the rights and privileges
of Masonry except those which are incident to membership in a
particular Lodge ( R.D. 926), and the brother's former Lodge
is left with no Masonic procedure, for the collection of delinquent
dues (R.D. 535).
3. The number of suspensions for non~payment of dues greatly
exceeds the number of suspensions and expulsions for unMasonk
conduct. The proposed amendments, therefore, would unlock
and unleash upon Grand Lodge a veritable Pandora's Box of
troubles and burdens in the form of ·petitions for restoration on
the part of brothers whose petitions for good cause have been
denied by their own Lodges. The constituent Lodges are in a

. 358 ·

359

PROCEEDINGS OP THE

GRAND LODGE OP CALIFORNIA

better position to determine the merits of a petition for restoration than is Grand ·Lodge.
For the foregoing reasons, it is your Committee's opinion that the
practical detriments, which will surely result from the proposed amendments, far outweigh the .theoretical benefits which might possibly be
derived.
We, therefore, recommend that the Resolution be not adopted.
A motion to adopt the original resolution was defeated.

Your committee. in 1954, recommended, and the Grand Lodge
adopted, resolution continuing the suspension in effect until this ( 1955)
Communication.
The suspended Master has not accounted, and has not asked for
hearing on the suspension or for any review thheof.
A successor Master was regularly installed during the suspension.
We cannot permit the matter to pass without calling attention
to the suspended Master's persistent failure to comply with his obligation to account, and to the flaunting by him of orders from both the
Inspector and the Grand Master with reference thereto. Failure of
the Lodge to take action in the premises is unexplained.
We recommend that the Lodge be directed to forthwith report 'to
the incoming Grand Master, and that the latter be authorized to direct
such action as the condition may warrant.
Adopted.

AMENDMENT OF SECTION 175
In order to clarify the situation, when the institution of a new lodge
does not occur until after the expiration of the period for which the
petitioning members have paid dues, your committee recommends that
Section 175 be amended to read as follows:
Section 175. Upon the granting by the Grand Master of a dispensation for the formation of a new Lodge the membership of
any signer of the petition therefor in any other Lodge in this
jurisdiction, from which he has not already withdrawn, shall
ipso facto cease as of the date of institution: however, he shall
nevertheless be liable for and shall pay to such Lodge such unpaid dues as may have accrued between the date of his certificate
of standing in such Lodge and the date of the instituting of the
new Lodge.

1954 DECISION NO. 21 BY GRAND MASTER HARWELL
By his Decision No. 21, the Grand Master in 1954 (Proceedings,
page 84) answered "Yes" to the question, "Must the Charity Committee,
consisting of the Master and Wardens of the Lodge, report at stated
meetings payments made since the last stated meeting?" In connection
therewith, he reported suspension, until the 1954 Communication, of
the Master of the Lodge, as authorized by Subdivision 8, Section 34 of
our Ordinances.
Notwithstanding repeated urging by the Inspector and direction
by the Grand Master (with warnings as to the consequences of recalcitrancy) that he do so, the Master of the Lodge had failed and refused
to account for more than $4,000 of Lodge funds entrusted to him as a
member of the Charity Committee.
Your Committee made informal inquiry into the matter during the
1954 Communication. The inquiry was not participated in by the suspended Master and had none of the attributes of a hearing. Therefrom
it appeared that Lodge officers, the Inspector and the Grand Master
had discussed the matter with the Master before his suspension and
that he was fully aware of the seriousness of his delinquency and of
the consequences of recalcitrancy.

AMENDMENT OF SECTION 332
Your Committee on Jurisprudence to which has been referred resolution offered by Wm. T. Lisenby, Jr., Past Master of University Lodge
No. 394, providing that the following language in Section 332 of the
Ordinances be struck out, "and be imprisoned in pursuance thereof,"
begs to report as follows:
The language used in the Ordinance was designed to protect the
individual Mason from the consequences of conviction of a felony in
certain cases. For example, if this amendment were adopted, one guilty
of negligent homicide could be summarily expelled although no moral
turpitude was involved.
Therefore, your Committee is of the opinion that this would go too
far and that the proposed amendment should not be adopted.
A motion to adopt the original resolution was defeated.

ALTER NATE COMM ISSION ERS

A Resolution has been proposed to add a new section to the Ross
Digest to read as follows:
Alternat e Commissioners.
Section 299 (a) . Whenev er it shall appear likely, that the trial
cannot be concluded in one day, the Lodge may in the same manner and
at the same time elect two Alternat e Commissioners, who shall attend
througho ut the trial as members of the Commission, except that they
shall not be entitled to vote, unless called to act in lieu of a Commissioner,
as hereinaf ter provided. The Alternat e Commissioner, who shall have
received the larger number of votes, shall be called first to replace a
Commissioner who may become disqualified to act as such during the
trial. In the event .that both Alternat es shall have received the same
number of votes, the Master shall decide who will be called first. An
Alternat e Commissioner may not replace a disqualified Commissioner,
unless he shall have been present at all times during the trial.
This proposal is designed to apply to Masonic trial procedure, provisions similar to those used in our Trial Courts in jury cases. While
it is probable that the principal involved in this proposed amendment
has merit, there are certain features which warrant further consideration
of its procedural effects. The Committee on Grievances is working
on a proposed revision of our whole trial procedur e and it is the opinion
of the Committee on Jurisprudence that it would be better to carry out
the revision as a whole than to amend our procedur e piecemeal at this
time. We, therefore, recommend that the proponen ts of the measure
present their views to the Committee on Grievances and that the pr~­
posed amendment be not adopted at this time.
A motion to adopt the original resolution was defeated .

CERTIF IED MAIL

The Grand Master in Decision No. 62 has ruled that service by
certified mail is not now permissible under Section 257 and Section 308
of the Ordinanc es. This Committee has concurre d in that Decision.
He has also recommended that said Section be amended to make the
use of certified mail deliverable to the addresse e only permissible. We.
therefore. recommend that Section 257 of the Ordinan ces be amended
to read as follows:
Sec. 257. In case any member shall have refused or neglected to
pay his regular dues during a period of twelve months, the Secretary shall notify him, either by registere d letter or certified
mail, deliverable to addresse e only, deposited in the U. S. Post
Office addresse d to him at his last known address, or by actual
service of notice, duly certified by the Tiler, that unless at the
next stated meeting either his dues be paid, or sickness or in·
ability to pay be shown as the cause of such refusal or neglect,
he will be suspende d from all rights and privileges of Masonry.

361

The Committee further recommends that Section 308 of the Ordinances be amended to read as follows:
Sec. 308. If the accused be within the jurisdiction of the Lodge,
the summons and copy of the charges shall be issued and served
upon the accused at least ten days prior to the day appointed for
the trial, and shall be served personally by the Tiler or some other
member of the Lodge authorized by the Master for that purpose,
or shall be left at his ordinary residence or place of business. If
he be without the said jurisdiction, but within the State, and his
· residence be known, they shall be issued and served upon the accused at least thirty days before the day of the trial. and shall
be forwarde d to his address by the Secretar y, by mail or other
usual mode of conveyance, and service shall be complete from
and after depositing the same in the mail upon due proof thereof.
If he be without the State, and his residence be known, they shall
be issued and served upon the accused at least ninety days before the trial, by the Secretar y forwardi ng the same to his address by certified mail deliverable to the addresse e only or United
States mail with •postage thereon prepaid, which shall be sufficient
service: or substitut ed service may be made by the Secretar y
forwarding such summons and copy of the charges by registered
mail addresse d to the accused at his actual or last known place of
residence, provided the return receipt shows the genuine signature of the accused. If his address be unknown, the Master shall
order the trial to proceed at once upon the testimony, ex parte.
In the event the trial shall be held ex parte, the record shall con.tain a full !l,tatement of the facts constituting due diligence in the
effort to locate the accused.
Adopted . 5/6 vote.

BUILDING AND LOAN INVESTMENTS
The Resolution presented by Brother John R. Moore, Past Master
of Meridian Lodge No. 667, reads as follows:
RESOLVED: That Ross Digest be amended by inserting the language quoted below as subparagraph E under subsection 1 of Sec. 86
and 1as subparagraph ( e) under ·subsection 1 of Sec. 152.1 :
.
"Investment certificates issued by a building and loan association or a savings and loan association organized and existing
under the laws of the State of California which is an insured
institution as defined by Title IV of the National Housing Act,
and shares issued by any such association which issues no invest-

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

363

ment ·certificates and which is an insured institution as defined by
said Title IV, and shares issued by any federal savings and loan
association; but in the ·case of each association only to the extent
that such investment certificates or shares are insured by the
Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation."
This resolution has merit and is approved for the following reasons:
Under our existing law as recently construed by our Grand Master
neither shares nor certificates issued by state or federal building or
savings and loan associations are eligible for investment of Lodge funds,
or Grand Lodge funds.
This amendment would therefore eliminate the discrimination which
now exists against the securities of such state and federal associations.
All federal savings and loan associations are insured institutions .
Since the amendment is limited to securities issued by insured institutions and to the types of securities which are insured, the suggested
amendment is conservative in its character.
The Grand Master put the vote but delayed announcing the result
pending the taking of a rising vote. On completion of the rising vote,
the Grand Master declared that a majority of the votes cast favored the
resolution, but the necessary 5/6 vote had not been passed in favor
thereof. He declared the resolution rejected at this Communication of
Grand Lodge, but in accordance with Section 28 of the Constitution,
held over to be again voted on at the 1956 Communication.

San Francisco,,California
Gentlemen:
We have examined the Balance Sheet of the
MASONIC HOMES OF CALIFORNIA
(A California Non-Profit Corporation)
as of July 31, 1955, and the related Statement of Revenue and Expenses for
the year then ended. In connection therewith we also examined the Balance
Sheets of the PERMANENT ENDOWMENT FUND and the other Endowment Funds of the Masonic Homes of California as of July 31, 1955, and
thefr related statements of revenue for the year then ended. Our examination was made in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards,
and accordingly included such tests of the accounting records and such other
auditing procedures as we considered necessary in the circwnstances.
The annual financial statements of the Masonic Homes of California
have been prepared for many years past on the cash basis of accounting,
modified to recognize minor accruaJs, and the attached financial statements
are prepared on the same basis.
In accordance with action taken by Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California at the 1953 Annual Communication confirming legal title to the
Permanent Endowment Fund of the Masonic Homes in the Masonic Homes
of California, the report on the audit of the Permanent Endowment Fund and
the John and Lena Luckenbach Fund are included in this report. In previous years the audit of these Funds was reported upon in a separate report.
The total revenue received by the Masonic Homes of California during
the fiscal year ended July 31, 1955, amounted to $654,158.51, as shown on
Exhibit D. Its operating expenses for the year amounted. to $6~8,805.81,
leaving a balance of unexpended revenue of $5,352.70. Capital gams irom
sales of securities in the amount of $90,554.93, and a refund of prior years
fire insurance premium of $9,281.21, resulted in a final net revenue for the
year of $105,188.84, as shown on Exhibit D. This revenue has been added to
the Capital of Masonic Homes of California.
General Fund cash on hand and on deposit in banks at July 31, 1955, as
shown iby Exhibit A, amounted to $889,695.23, an increase of $346, 785.21 over
the amount on hand and on deposit at the beginnin,g of the year.
The total amount of the General Fund invested in securities at July 31,
1955 amounted to $1,097,276.87, as shown on Exhibit A. Securities purchased are stated on the books and in this report at cost. Securities received
as donations are stated at market value when received or at the nominal
value of $1.00, if the market value was not known.
The amount of $81,924.24 shown as notes and contracts receivable on
Exhibit A is the result of sales of real estate received by the Masonic Homes
of California by assignment from applicants admitted to the Home at Decoto.
The value of land, buildings, and equipment is shown on Exhibit A, at
$3,094,449.33, ~e cost when originally P'!ll"i;hased. IJ?- ~cordance w~th the
consistent policy of the Trustees, depreciation of buildmgs. a!ld · e9wpment
is not provided for in the ac~ounts, bu~ replacements of origm~l. items are
considered expenses of operations. Durmg the current year additions to. the
Decoto Home were $75,087.00 for elevators, $10,017.97 for wells and pumps,
and $3,513.09 for a new kitchen. Additions to the Covina Home were

The Other Assets of $3,294.48 shown on Exhibit A, consist of real estate
and life insurance policies assigned to Masonic Homes of California by residents of the Decoto Home. The individual parcels of real estate and life
insurance policies are each recorded at the nominal value of $1.00 for accountability, with the exception that payments by Masonic Homes of California on loans obtained by the assignors of such policies are added to the
nominal values. The proceeds from the sale of this real estate and from the
life insurance policies are credited direct to one of the Reserves for Special
Purposes as directed by the Trustess.
The sundry liabilities of $6,895.17, shown on Exhibit A, consists of
$4,3~8.44 of accounts payable ~Y ~e Covina Home, and $2,506.73 representing the amount of the contri:butions of employees of the Masonic Homes
payable to Wells Fargo Bank as. Trustee under the "Masonic Homes of
California Retirement Income Plan".
The "Masonic Homes of California Retirement Income Plan", was authorized at the 1947 Annual Communication of Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. This
plan became effective January 1, 1955. "The object of the Plan is to provide
a method whereby Masonic Homes of California and its employees may make
regular contributions to a trust fund to provide definite retirement income
benefits for participating employees who become entitled thereto." Under
the terms of the Plan participating employees contribute 3% of their regular
salary which is deposited by the Masonic Homes with the Wells Fargo Bank
as Trustee. Under the terms of the Plan the Masonic Homes may make
voluntary contributions to the trust fund in order to place the Plan on a
sound actuarial basis. According to Coates, Herfurth & England, Consulting Actuaries, employed by the Masonic Homes, there is a past service
liability to be funded by the Masonic Homes in the amount of $58,068.00,
and the present value of benefits to be provided by future contributions of
the Masonic Homes ·a mounts to $173,829.00. The Masonic Homes has, to
date, contributed a token .. 100.00 to the Trustee. No additional contributions are contemplated until the Plan has received the approval of the Internal Revenue Service.
The Trustees of the Masonic Homes have established six special reserves
to which are credited the amounts of donations and bequests which are to
be used for purposes other than direct operating expenses. These reserves,
representing funds aggregating $1,344,367.40 at July 31, 1955, are shown on
the attached Balance Sheet as "Reserves for Special Purposes". The activities of these reserves during the year are shown on Schedule 4.
Endowment funds held by the Masonic Homes of California amounted

to a total of $6,825,548.97 at July 31, 1955, as shown by Exhibit A. Of these
funds $6,282,548.95 was in the Permanent Endowment Fund of Masonic

Homes of California. The Permanent Endowment Fund was increased by
$748,208.73 during the current year by donations, bequests, gains on securities sold, and $100,000.00 transferred from the Covina Special Fund. The
other endowment funds increased during the year by the aggregate sum of
$37,249.77. A description of each of the endowment funds, together with a
Balance Sheet, and, where appropriate, a statement of the related revenue,
is shown on Exhibits E to M, inclusive.

In our opinion, subject to the foregoing comments, the accompanying
Balance Sheet, marked Exhibit A, and the related Statement of Revenue
and Expenses, marked Exhibit D, together with the balance sheets of the
Endowment Funds and the related statements of revenue, present fairly,
on the cash basis of accounting, the financial position of the Masonic Homes
of California and its Endowment F~ds at July 31, 1955, and the results of

MEMORIAL TEMPLE AUDIT
August 29,1955
To the Trustees of the California Masonic Memorial Temple
Masonic Temple
25 Van Ness Avenue
San Francisco, California
Gentlemen:
We have examined the balance sheet of the CALIFORNIA MASONIC
MEMORIAL TEMPLE (a California Non-Profit Corporation) as of July 31,
1955, and the related statement of income and expenses for the year then
ended. We have also examined the records of the building operations as
maintained by James Hurst Co., in its capacity as property managers. Our
examination was made in accordance with generally accepted auditing
standards, and accordingly included such tests of the accounting records and
such other auditing procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances.
The California Masonic Memorial Temple was incoryorated under the
"General Non-Profit Corporation Law" of the State of California on January
6, 1954. Its primary purpose is to hold title to that certain real property upon
which a building to ·b e known as the California Masonic Memorial Temple is
to be erected, to collect income therefrom, and to turn over the entire amount
thereof, less expenses, to the Endowment Fund of Masonic Homes of California, a charitable non-profit corporation.
'
Contributions received during the fiscal year ended July 31, 1955, for the
erection of the new memorial temple amounted to $728,181.57, which amount
has been added to the capital of the Corporation as shown on Exhibit A.
Net income from operations during the year amounted to $15,017.63, as shown
by Exhibit B. Thus, contributions and net income provided total funds during
the year of $743.199.20. Of this amount $103,500.00 was used to pay off the
balance of the mortgage on the temple site, $351.92 was expended for costs
incident to the new temple, and the balance of $639,347.28 was added to the
amount on deposit in banks, thus increasing that amount from $400,183.78 as
at July 31, 1954, to $1,039,531.06 at July 31, 1955, as shown on Exhibit A.
The total contributions received to July 31, 1955, for the erection of the
new memorial temple, amounted to $1,768,337.12. Of this amount $939,628.55
represents contributions received from individual Masons subsequent to
August 1, 1953. Contributions from individual Masons are collected by the
California Masonic Memorial Temple Committee of the Grand Lodge,
F. & A. M., and are immediately turned over to the Memorial Temple corporation. The Committee reports unpaid contribution pledges at July 31,
1955, of approximaaely $195,000.00. Unpaid pledges are not taken into account
as an asset by the Memorial Temple corporation until collected by-the Committee and turned over to it. The entire amount collected on pledges will be
available for the cost of erecting the new temple inasmuch as all the expenses
of the Temple Committee are paid from funds appropriated out of the revenues of Grand Lodge, F. & A. M.
The audit report for the previous year was prepared on a modified
accrual basis of accounting. ThJS report for the current year ended July 31,
1955, has been preJ?ared on the cash basis of accounting, the basis upon which
the annual financial statements of the Grand Lodge F. & A. M. and the
Masonic Homes of California are prepared. The change in accounting method
required a retroactive adjustment reducing the net loss as shown for the year
ended July 31 1954, by the amount of $1,598.87. Otherwise the change in
accounting haa1 no significant effect upon the financial statements appearing
in this report.
There were no unpaid liabilities at the end of the year other than current
bills of a nominal amount in connection with the operation of the properties
and legal and organization expense not in excess of $3,000 in connection
with the formation of the Memorial Temple corporation. The only material

415
